author: Ryan McLaughlin
title: High school baseball: Stalwart pitching has young, talented GSA club off to strong start | Sports | ellsworthamerican.com
text:
Charlie Sullivan had a strong feeling that the George Stevens Academy baseball team was going to be a contender in Class C North this spring.
With the regular season only four games old, the Eagles are looking very much like one.
While GSA's pitching has been strong behind brothers Spencer and Wyatt Young, coach Dan Kane's Eagles got their bats going Wednesday afternoon in a 13-1 victory over Orono at the University of Maine.
The Eagles have won their first four contests, including two victories over the Red Riots.
GSA pushed across nine runs in the top of the fifth inning to open the floodgates on what had been a 4-1 game, and Wyatt Young was dominant on the mound in allowing one run on just two hits while striking out 10 in five innings.
The game ended after the fifth inning due to the 10-run mercy rule.
As the Eagles' catcher, Sullivan has seen first-hand just how stellar GSA's pitching has performed.
"We knew we were going to be better than last year," said Sullivan. "We're definitely confident right now. Our pitching has been good."
Wyatt Young was certainly dialed in Wednesday, as he retired the first nine Red Riots while exhibiting strong command in issuing only one walk.
The fourth inning, in which Orono scored its one run, was the only frame in which the Red Riots had any baserunners.
"I threw a lot of fastballs and I [knew] I could throw strikes today and it ended up going pretty well," Young said.
Kane had been waiting for his offense to break loose, and it did just that on a chilly, breezy afternoon.
Spencer Young opened the scoring for the Eagles by ripping an RBI single in the top of the third while Sullivan's looping two-run single to right keyed GSA's three-run third.
"We did hit some balls extremely hard today," Kane said. "I'm very proud of how they swung the bats today. Wyatt Young absolutely crushed the ball three times."
GSA pounded out seven hits and took advantage of three Red Riot errors in scoring nine times in the top of the fifth to force the mercy rule.
Wyatt Young's triple to deep center field was the spark plug for that rally, while the Eagles got contributions from multiple players.
Clancy Chittenden ripped a two-run single down the left field line and Max Eckenfelder and Noah Grindal each roped run-scoring base hits.
Wyatt Young struck out the side in the last of the fifth to finish the game.
The Eagles are young but talented and played a lot of freshmen last spring, but were quick to get to work last offseason, which Kane noted has been the biggest difference.
"We're finally growing up, last year we were a team with a lot of freshmen," he said. "They did their job in the offseason and worked hard at their game, and as you can see it's paying off."
The Eagles do understand that a baseball season is a marathon, not a sprint, and they want to be playing their best ball in late May and early June.
"We just need to get as a team a little bit more," Sullivan said.
"Every game so far we've made some mistakes so we're trying to clean those things up most of the time," Kane said.
